ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks which Lids are fuel and which are savings, and the late game grows through Spring cascades and Mabyn's Patience payout; the early turns are thinner, since Patience rarely pays before Tier 3.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: Lids don't count as units for attack order or the front row, so a front row of doors sends enemy attacks into your back row, and scouts see only Knocks. No current tribe or generic auto-battler hides its fighting board like that.

verdict_why: The v3 rule lines now read cleanly and each tier does its job; more passes would mostly move numbers, which the owner balances afterwards.

points.text: Ballooning Money Spider seldom turns Patient early, because a small Lodge board has to open its Lids to fight. A small bonus when it Springs would give the Tier 1 seed a job on either path.

The chain build's only lasting growth is Dew Gallery Orbweaver (plus Silk-Apron Sponsor once). A Tier 5 card that banks part of this fight's Springs as permanent stats would give Sprung Trap a late-game shape to match Patience.
Gossamer Jill's Spiderlings also push the Orbweaver, Ballot Clerk and Worshipful Master counts, which makes her the bridge between the two builds. Worth keeping as the tribe's top-end hinge.
Cork-Lid Doorward could name its target (the biggest unit that Sprang) so players can plan which strike repeats, rather than it going to whoever Springs first.

standouts.why: Slit-Mender Purseweb stabs the enemy across before each of its attacks and closes again: a clear, satisfying trap that grows through the fight.
Grand Tyler Mabyn Underlid is a real Tier 6 payoff that turns a winning streak of shut doors into a big board.
Signora Corkhinge gives a reason to hide a strong unit: her aura feeds every Spring from a place no enemy can reach.

weakest.why: Usher of the Degrees gives only +2/+2 at Tier 3; its Lid-granting is good for cross-tribe boards but low output for the slot.
Ballooning Money Spider's Patience payout rarely starts before the mid game.
Wafer-Lid Nemesia needs three friendly deaths, so it often opens after the fight is decided.

flags.note: Mabyn and Old Diadem both pay on Patience, and shut Lids count as survivors for hero damage, so a win streak makes the board grow and hit harder each round. One loss resets it, which is the counterplay.
With Corkhinge and The Past Master, each Slit-Mender stab gains +6 Attack and +4/+4 before landing, and since a kill cancels the enemy's attack, the unit across may never get to swing.
Worshipful Master replays Springs from units that re-closed (Slit-Mender, Doorward targets); check that a replayed Spring from under a Lid behaves as intended and doesn't stack with the re-close.
